data: Carried Sputnik and Gagarin to orbit
Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.
Wikipedia Vostok-L infobox: 30.84 m; Astronautix vostok8k72 30.84 m x 2.99 m — dimensions

The launcher that put Sputnik in orbit in 1957 and Yuri Gagarin into space in 1961. A direct ancestor of every Soyuz rocket flown since — the longest production lineage in spaceflight, with thousands of flights across six decades.
First artificial satellite to orbit Earth — start of the Space Age
Sputnik 1 (1957). Vostok 1 — Gagarin (1961). Five hundred and forty Soyuz launches from a single pad.
Soviet R-7-derived launcher that put Gagarin in space — Vostok 1 (1961-04-12) and 5 more Vostok flights through 1963
Vostok-K successor — more thrust for the heavier Voskhod capsule. Launched Voskhod 1 (1964) + Voskhod 2 (1965 Leonov EVA)
R-7-derived launcher for the first-generation Soyuz spacecraft — flew Soyuz 1 (1967) and Soyuz 11 (1971)
The Soviet / Russian heavy-lift workhorse 1967-2012 — Salyut, Mir, Venera, Vega, Luna sample-return
Soviet Moon rocket; four launches all failed
